note: One fixed, heavy, technical prompt, held constant across every style iteration. It is deliberately multi-part so the final message has to carry links, verbatim errors, a comparison, numbers and a next step all at once — the whole readability rubric in one run.
prompt: The gateway is throwing 503s and I'm the one on call. Everything you need is in this directory. Work out what actually happened from logs/gateway.log, logs/worker.log and deploys.csv, then give me the on-call handoff. I need all of this: the exact timestamp the failures start and the error line word for word; what the connection pool numbers were doing right before and right after that; which deploy lines up with it, and which of the other deploys are red herrings and why; whether the workers took the same hit or whether this is gateway-only, with the evidence either way; the impact window and roughly how many failed requests it covers; and the single thing I should do right now.

groundTruth.note: Every figure here was read out of the fixture. A claim the message makes that this does not mention is not a contradiction — only a claim that conflicts with something stated here is.
groundTruth.root_cause: Deploy dep-4471 (service gateway, author a.novak, 02:12:00Z to 02:14:00Z, summary "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation") applied config generation 119, which flipped gateway.pool.perRequest from false to true. Taking a connection per request exhausted the fixed 20-connection pool.
groundTruth.config_change_applied_at: 2026-03-14T02:13:41.234Z. Logged as generation 119 applied, 3 keys changed: "gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true", "gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500", and "gateway.log.sampleRate: 1.0 -> 1.0" which is a no-op change to the same value.
groundTruth.first_failure: 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z, req-07401. Two lines at that timestamp: "ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms" and "ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)". A slow-acquire WARN for req-07400 precedes it at 02:14:14.920Z.
groundTruth.gap_between_config_and_first_failure: The config applied at 02:13:41.234Z and the first 503 is at 02:14:18.972Z, so the gap is 37.7 seconds. Anything in the range of roughly 35 to 40 seconds is correct. Measuring instead from the deploy finishing at 02:14:00Z gives about 19 seconds, which is also defensible if the message says that is what it measured.
groundTruth.impact_window: Starts 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z. Still failing at the last line of the log, 2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z. About one hour and forty-five minutes, and unresolved. The log header says node-3 of 3, so it covers one node.
groundTruth.failed_request_count: Exactly 530 lines match "ERROR access ... 503" and exactly 530 lines match ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED. A count of 530 is correct. A count derived from grepping the string "503" alone gives 548 and is wrong, because it also matches request ids and latencies.
groundTruth.pool_before: Before the change the periodic "INFO pool stats" lines read size=20 with in_use oscillating roughly between 3 and 11, idle making up the rest, and waiting=0 throughout.
groundTruth.pool_after: After the change every stats line reads size=20 in_use=20 idle=0, and waiting climbs steadily: 12 at 02:15:58Z, 32 at 02:20:58Z, 132 at 03:45:58Z, 152 at 03:50:58Z, 172 at 03:55:58Z. Individual ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED lines report waiting counts up to 232. The pool never recovers.
groundTruth.workers: logs/worker.log has zero ERROR and zero FATAL lines and no 503s. Every job logs "finished ok". Its own pool is separate and smaller, and every stats line from 01:00:55Z to 03:50:55Z reads size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0, flat throughout. Job durations do climb across the window, from about 200ms to about 2300ms, while db_wait stays between 0ms and 12ms. There is one unrelated WARN at 02:36:22.838Z about a slow unindexed query, already tracked as OPS-2210. This was gateway-only.
groundTruth.red_herrings: dep-4468 (catalog-svc, 22:04Z on Mar 13) and dep-4469 (accounts-svc, 23:31Z on Mar 13) are hours early and on other services. dep-4470 (worker, 00:48Z) is over an hour early and the workers never failed. dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) both ship after the failures already started, so neither can be the cause. The OPS-2210 slow query is a known pre-existing issue.
groundTruth.correct_next_action: Roll back dep-4471, or revert gateway.pool.perRequest to false. Nothing else in the evidence points anywhere useful. No worker action is needed.
